microtheory.name: object_recognition_vision
microtheory.definition: How visual input becomes object identification. Feature integration, view invariance, structural description, deep network models. Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept-extraction from visual input.

concepts.name: structural_description_theory
concepts.definition: Marr + Biederman. Object recognition via decomposition into 3D primitives + their spatial relations. Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional object model.

concepts.name: geon
concepts.definition: Biederman 1987. Generalized cone primitives: cylinder, cone, brick, wedge. ~36 geons combine to ~30000 objects. Substrate analogue: substrate's visual-feature primitives.

concepts.name: recognition_by_components
concepts.definition: RBC. Biederman. Objects = configurations of geons. Substrate analogue: substrate's parts-relational object model.

concepts.name: view_based_theory
concepts.definition: Bülthoff + Edelman. Objects stored as collection of 2D views. Recognition via interpolation. Substrate analogue: substrate's view-collection-based recognition.

concepts.name: feature_integration_theory_object
concepts.definition: Treisman 1980. Features detected pre-attentively; binding into objects requires attention. Substrate analogue: substrate's attention-binding mechanism.

concepts.name: viewpoint_invariance
concepts.definition: Recognize same object from different angles. Substrate analogue: substrate's view-collapse mechanism.

concepts.name: scale_invariance
concepts.definition: Recognize same object at different sizes. Substrate analogue: substrate's scale-normalization.

concepts.name: translation_invariance
concepts.definition: Same identity regardless of position. Substrate analogue: substrate's position-pooling.

concepts.name: illumination_invariance
concepts.definition: Recognize despite lighting changes. Substrate analogue: substrate's lighting-discounted identity.

concepts.name: feature_hierarchy_visual
concepts.definition: Hubel + Wiesel + extensions. Edges → contours → parts → objects. Each level pools over lower. Substrate analogue: substrate's hierarchical genlMt.

concepts.name: complex_cell_pooling
concepts.definition: V1 complex cells pool over position to gain translation invariance. Substrate analogue: substrate's translation-pooling mechanism.

concepts.name: hmax_model
concepts.definition: Riesenhuber + Poggio. Alternating S (selectivity) + C (pooling) layers building invariance. Substrate analogue: substrate's alternating selectivity + pooling architecture.

concepts.name: face_recognition
concepts.definition: Specialized system. FFA (fusiform face area). Holistic processing — face as gestalt. Bruce + Young model. Substrate analogue: substrate's specialized-category recognition.

concepts.name: face_inversion_effect
concepts.definition: Inverted faces are much harder to recognize than inverted objects. Shows holistic processing. Substrate analogue: substrate's gestalt-required category.

concepts.name: prosopagnosia
concepts.definition: Face-recognition deficit despite intact object recognition. Localized FFA damage. Substrate analogue: substrate's domain-specific deficit.

concepts.name: object_constancy
concepts.definition: Stable object identity across views, distances, lighting. Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent-Concept-across-transformation.

concepts.name: object_permanence
concepts.definition: Knowing object exists when occluded. Substrate analogue: substrate's persistent-Mt across input gaps.

concepts.name: amodal_completion
concepts.definition: Perceiving occluded parts of objects. Substrate analogue: substrate's pattern-completion across occlusion.

concepts.name: convolutional_neural_network
concepts.definition: CNN. LeCun 1989. Convolutional + pooling layers. Translates invariance + parameter sharing. Foundation of modern computer vision. Substrate analogue: substrate's local-pattern + position-invariant processing.

concepts.name: imagenet_breakthrough
concepts.definition: AlexNet 2012. CNNs surpassed traditional methods. Started deep learning revolution. Substrate analogue: substrate's emergent visual recognition.

concepts.name: transfer_learning_vision
concepts.definition: Networks trained on large datasets fine-tune to specific tasks with little data. Substrate analogue: substrate's foundational visual Mt transfer.

concepts.name: adversarial_examples
concepts.definition: Small perturbations of input causing misclassification. Reveals fragility of CNN representations. Substrate analogue: substrate's failure modes under tiny shifts.

concepts.name: vision_transformer
concepts.definition: Dosovitskiy 2020. Transformer on image patches. Competes with CNNs. Substrate analogue: substrate's attention-based visual processing.

concepts.name: object_detection
concepts.definition: Locate + classify objects in scene. YOLO, R-CNN, DETR. Substrate analogue: substrate's spatial Concept localization.

concepts.name: instance_segmentation
concepts.definition: Pixel-level localization of each object instance. Mask R-CNN. Substrate analogue: substrate's pixel-Concept assignment.

concepts.name: semantic_segmentation
concepts.definition: Pixel-level category assignment (not instances). FCN, U-Net. Substrate analogue: substrate's pixel-category map.

concepts.name: image_classification
concepts.definition: Assign category to whole image. Classic ImageNet task. Substrate analogue: substrate's image-level Concept assignment.

rules.name: objects_are_parts_in_relation
rules.head: the substrate recognises an object
rules.body: the representation is parts (geons or features) in structural relation, not a holistic template. Biederman 1987. Substrate's compositional object.

rules.name: invariance_built_through_pooling
rules.head: the substrate must recognize objects across transformations
rules.body: pooling operations (max, average) over spatial/scale/rotation neighborhoods build invariance. Substrate's pooling-based invariance.

rules.name: faces_processed_holistically
rules.head: the substrate processes a face
rules.body: it's recognized as gestalt — features in relation, not separately. Inversion disrupts this. Substrate's holistic-processing category.

rules.name: context_speeds_recognition
rules.head: the substrate sees an object in a typical scene context
rules.body: scene context primes the expected category. Faster + more accurate recognition. Substrate's context-conditioned Concept activation.

rules.name: adversarial_perturbations_reveal_representation_limits
rules.head: the substrate's recognition can be fooled by tiny input perturbations
rules.body: the representation doesn't capture true object structure. Substrate's failure-mode probing.
